findings.text: Exposes read side release entry points for normal fast fast updown and NMI safe flavors plus notrace variants. Normal and NMI safe forms identify the critical section by a small integer index while fast forms identify it by a per CPU counter handle for the calling CPU. Each release ends the matching acquisition in the same domain.

Ending a fast updown critical section always accounts exactly one matching unlock against its lock and must not allow the protected region to leak past the release. The tiny configuration delegates to the common index based release after deriving the index from the supplied counter handle while the tree configuration records the unlock directly in the per CPU counter for the current CPU using NMI safe accounting where the build requires it.

No additional ordering barrier is required immediately after opening or closing an SRCU read side critical section because the lock and unlock primitives themselves already provide the needed full ordering. The explicit after lock and after unlock helpers therefore have no effect.

Provides scoped guard constructors that automatically pair acquisition and release for SRCU domains in the normal fast fast notrace and fast updown flavors. Declaring a guard variable of the requested flavor ensures the critical section is closed when the scope exits.

Tiny configuration domain object holds a pair of nesting depths indexed by reader generation, run and wait indicators for grace period activity, current and maximum requested index values, a wait queue used to wake a grace period waiter on final release, head and tail linkage for pending callbacks, separate deferred work objects for process and interrupt context progress, and optional dependency state for debug builds.

Statically declared tiny domains start with an empty callback queue whose tail link points at the head slot, an initialized wait queue, process work bound to the grace period driver and interrupt work bound to its tiny handler, plus dependency initialization where applicable. All static declaration helpers for normal fast and fast updown flavors produce the same initial state in this configuration differing only in storage duration.

In the tiny configuration there is no separate update side allocation so usage state is empty and its initializer is vacuous. Dynamic initialization for fast and fast updown flavors aliases the common initialization and no distinct sizing or combining structure is required.

Tiny configuration offers an expedited grace period wait that carries identical semantics to the normal wait. Callers requesting expedited completion receive the same guarantee as the standard operation without a distinct fast path.

Tiny active reader detection reports busy whenever either generation nesting count is nonzero. Diagnostic reporting derives the current generation from the stored index value and summarizes both nesting counts together with current and furthest index progression for torture observation.

Tree per generation counter object holds two monotonically increasing tallies one for entries and one for exits maintained with atomic long semantics to allow concurrent updates from multiple contexts on the same CPU.

Tree per CPU state pairs read side generation counters for both index values with a recorded reader flavor and update side machinery comprising a private spin lock a segmented callback list needed sequence numbers for normal and expedited work an invoking flag a delay timer and work context for callback execution dedicated callback heads for barrier and expedite current operations with associated expedite state a back link to the leaf combining node with group mask plus CPU identity and domain back pointer.

Combining tree node carries its own private spin lock four generation indexed sequence values recording children with pending callbacks four matching bit sets identifying which per CPU states hold callbacks for each generation a furthest needed expedited sequence a parent link and the inclusive CPU range covered by the node.

Tree update side shared state anchors the combining tree through node base and per level entry points tracks small to large transition progress serializes callback preparation and grace period work with dedicated mutexes while protecting counters and size state with a private spin lock holds grace period sequence state including current and needed normal and expedited values with start and end timestamps contention measurement interval and event counts static allocation marker barrier sequencing with mutex completion and remaining CPU count rescheduling controls delayed and interrupt work items and a back pointer to the owning domain.

Tree domain object is a small header pointing at per CPU counter storage and per CPU data arrays recording the required reader flavor carrying lock dependency state and referencing shared update side state. It contains no inline grace period or callback storage itself.

Small to large sizing uses nine ordered values from zero through eight where zero denotes no combining tree one denotes allocation in progress two denotes tree adoption pending barrier three denotes adoption pending call handling four through seven denote progressive callback visibility initialization across the four generation slots and eight denotes a fully initialized large tree.

Size control advances monotonically from small with no tree through allocation then through staged adoption where barrier handling call handling and callback array initialization complete in order reaching the large stable state only after all four callback slots are trusted. No transition moves backward toward small in the observed definitions.
Reader state scanning distinguishes three values with zero for idle and one and two for first and second scan passes.
Expedite current handling distinguishes three values with zero for idle one for pending request and two for repost required.

Initial grace period sequence is positioned one hundred periods before zero in the counter field with a companion value one less to represent the with state variant used for needed tracking at startup.

Tree static construction creates paired usage and domain objects with usage sequence state preset to the initial values unlocked protection and empty delayed work. Domain wiring always links the usage object records the requested flavor and initializes dependency tracking with in tree builds further linking per CPU data and counter base while modular builds register the domain pointer in a dedicated section for later per CPU attachment. Flavor selection encodes normal as zero and distinct codes for fast and fast updown with static versus external linkage as the only other difference.

Conversion between a per CPU counter handle and its generation index is bijective relative to the domain per CPU base. Deriving an index from a handle yields the offset from the base slot and deriving a handle from an index yields the corresponding slot address for the current CPU data.

Tree active reader detection aggregates across all possible CPUs and both generations by summing entry tallies and subtracting exit tallies. A nonzero aggregate indicates readers still present while zero indicates quiescence.

Torture framework exposes helpers to declare module parameters with descriptive text and to emit tagged log lines for normal verbose conditional and error reporting. Verbose output is suppressed unless verbosity is enabled with a sleep to avoid flooding while error output carries distinctive marking.

Torture initialization failure handling warns once when built in and the supplied error is negative returning true exactly in the failure case. The online CPU query in this configuration always reports a single CPU and offline handling uses a simple callback type taking no arguments and returning nothing.
Torture random state pairs an unsigned evolution value with a signed iteration count. Helpers provide static zero initialized instances for global and per CPU use.
Random state initialization resets both the evolution value and the iteration count to zero.

Torture thread control offers creation with automatic naming and status messages an extended form accepting a completion callback and a stop helper that announces termination. All forms delegate to common internal create and stop primitives while threading through the caller task pointer.
Torture voluntary preemption has two build dependent forms one invoking the scheduler preemption entry and one expanding to an empty statement that performs no action.

Tracing for this subsystem uses the rcu domain name with event definition aliasing either to the active event macro or to a no operation placeholder depending on build configuration. Torture names are limited to eight characters.

Sequence values pack a grace counter with a small state field. Helpers extract the counter and state portions replace the state portion with validation and bracket update side work with start and end operations that advance the value and enforce ordering. End value computation rounds the current value up to the next full period boundary.

Snapshot captures the next full period boundary beyond the current value with ordering that prevents bleeding into the critical section while current simply observes the stored value. Started and done tests compare a snapshot against the evolving value using wraparound safe ordering with an exact variant that also tolerates very old snapshots from prior wrap cycles.

Completion helpers determine whether a new observation has advanced beyond an older one at period granularity distinguishing any completed period from a newly started one and estimate how many full periods separate two observations with rounding that treats partial periods conservatively.
State query uses bit one for completed and bit two for not tracked. One full grace increment equals the state mask plus one. Callback head debugging distinguishes ready as zero and queued as one.

Grace sequence state cycles from idle through busy back to idle at the next counter value. Start moves out of idle into busy end moves from busy to the next idle and direct state replacement is permitted only within the mask range.
Callback head debug tracking alternates between ready and queued. Queuing moves from ready to queued while activating debug state and unqueuing reverses from queued to ready while deactivating.

Debug tracking for callback queuing is build dependent. When enabled it activates the object and records transitions between ready and queued returning a status from the activation step and later reverses the transition and deactivates. When disabled both operations are vacuous with queuing reporting success.

Callback entry validates that a handler is present dumping object details on unexpected absence. Barrier completion is recognized by a self linked next pointer indicating the callback has already run.

Misuse is signaled rather than silently accepted. Supplying an index with bits beyond the low position entering normal release from NMI context or exiting fast updown while RCU is not watching each trigger a warning. Sequence helpers warn when a replacement state exceeds the mask or when start and end are invoked outside their expected busy states and callback handling treats a missing handler as suspicious.

Tree per CPU and node counters are guarded by private raw spin locks with update side shared state adding a spin lock for counters and sizing plus separate mutexes serializing callback preparation grace period work and barrier operations. Callback list and combining tree membership changes require holding the associated node or data lock. Read side critical sections are tracked as shared holdings on the domain with lock dependency state released on unlock and NMI safe release explicitly drops dependency tracking before completing.

Boot progress is queryable through a predicate reporting whether in kernel boot has finished. Stall reporting is suppressed only while a boot time suppression flag remains set and boot has not yet ended.
Each header defines a once only inclusion guard macro that prevents multiple processing of its declarations within a single translation unit.
